Q: How can I install packages offline? A:

As a continuation to chaokunyang's answer, I want to add the script here I wrote that does the work:

  1. Write a requirements.txt file that specifies the libraries you want to pack.

  2. Create a tar file that contains all your libraries (see the Packer script).

  3. Put the created tar file in the target machine and untar it.

  4. run the Installer script (which is also packed into the tar file).

requirements.txt file:

docker==4.4.0

Packer side: File name: create-offline-python3.6-dependencies-repository.sh:

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# This script follows the steps described in this link:
# https://stackoverflow.com/a/51646354/8808983

LIBRARIES_DIR="python3.6-wheelhouse"

if [ -d ${LIBRARIES_DIR} ]; then
    rm -rf ${LIBRARIES_DIR}/*
else
    mkdir ${LIBRARIES_DIR}
fi

pip download -r requirements.txt -d ${LIBRARIES_DIR}

files_to_add=("requirements.txt" "install-python-libraries-offline.sh")

for file in "${files_to_add[@]}"; do
    echo "Adding file ${file}"
    cp "$file" ${LIBRARIES_DIR}
done

tar -cf ${LIBRARIES_DIR}.tar ${LIBRARIES_DIR}

Installer side: file name: "install-python-libraries-offline.sh"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# This script follows the steps described in this link:
# https://stackoverflow.com/a/51646354/8808983

# This file should run during the installation process from inside the libraries directory, after it was untared:
# pythonX-wheelhouse.tar -> untar -> pythonX-wheelhouse
# |
# |--requirements.txt
# |--install-python-libraries-offline.sh

pip3 install -r requirements.txt --no-index --find-links .

Q: Why Does Trying to Load rJava Keep Resulting in an Error? A:

Ok, every solution to this problem seems to be unique so sorry to all the people who will Google this and find that this doesn't help, but here is what fixed it for me:

  1. I used rJavaEnv to install Java 21

  2. I added the following to my project's .Rprofile ([my username] here being a stand-in for my actual system profile username):

    dyn.load(
    x = "/home/[my username]/.cache/R/rJavaEnv/installed/linux/x64/21/lib/server/libjvm.so",
    local = T
)

  3. Running library(rJava) suddenly works just fine

Q: QML Module not installed (C++ backend) A:

Your qt_add_resources call is broken. As you missed the closing parenthesis, PREFIX and FILES are floating outside the function. Also, in Qt6 you don't need version numbers in QML imports, just use import art.sz instead of import art.sz 1.0. Once the module builds correctly, Qt will generate a qmldir file under your build directory’s QML output path.

Q: Is there a way to automatically import data into a form field in Adobe Acrobat Pro? A:

Adobe Acrobat will open a textfile.FDF as if it is a extension.PDF and that file will have the up to date data say from a Database or other program even a simple shell command or batch file.

The user opens that file of the day (or minute) with Adobe PDF Loader/Editor/Reader DC and it then automatically calls its /UF parent form / template.pdf.

There is no simpler method than open a child data file to call its parents data form. Form Data 001 loads the PDF for saving then Form Data 002 will change the contents for second save, this ability is programable in Acrobat DC or many other Command Line based FDF editor apps.

Another alternative is the user uses the Adobe import Forms Data File.

For bulk programming one file after another use an FDF Toolkit such as the one Adobe provided in the past.

Many PDF tools can blend an FDF with a Template.PDF but may be harder to find than PDFTK.

Q: Apache Nifi is not starting: Management Server Address System Property A:

Open <NIFI_HOME>\conf\bootstrap.conf and add a new java.arg line as java.arg.12=-Dorg.apache.nifi.management.server.address=127.0.0.1:9990.

Q: Calculating a Percent with a Filter on Text Dates A:

You have to make the divisible real and big at first:

select round(
      100.0 *
        (select count() from x where date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31')
        /
        (select count(*) from x)
    , 2)
